That's not a shadowban. A shadowban is used by admins. You don't even know you are banned on the site. Nothing you post or comment can be seen by the rest of the site.
Shadowbans were intended for spammers and advertisers. It was to make them think everyone could still see their comments so they wouldn't immediately create a new spammer account.
I know why it was implemented, but it evolved into something completely different. I just hope that Voat finds a way to implement a better or equal alternative.
voat is being pretty transparent about that kind of stuff, unlike reddit that just shadow bans for no reason with no logs

As a concept, shadow-banning is good. It helps fight spam bots by banning them without them knowing it. So they can keep posting with the same accounts instead of creating new ones once they detect they were banned.

The problem was that deaddit admins (the only ones capable of issuing shadow-bans) started miss-using this powerful tool and banning real people because of other reasons than spamming.

The other danger is automating the system, which if you're fighting spammers is tempting to do. Then normal users get caught up in this system, take a while to notice it, and then have limited avenues to appeal the shadowban.

I see what you mean but automating a system to get rid of spam is almost a necessity. There will be some false positives of course but worth an adequate appeal or reporting system they can be averted.

I think the problem is that it would require automation, and I don't think the false positives are worth it. Users who are incorrectly shadowbanned may take weeks to realize it. I don't think that the negatives are worth it, but I can certainly respect your stance since there are positives as well.
Shadowbans are a useful tool to combat bots and spammers.
